HBRIDGE command flow

The serial commands for one shot on the Limiter or the ECH-HVPS controller (both run the HBRIDGE firmware), in the order the controller accepts them, and the path out of a fault. Check the reply to each command before sending the next.

The hub logs and announces this as a dangerous command Fault path Phases U, V, W are channels 1, 2, 3

The shot is a list of setpoints

Time in whole microseconds, frequency in Hz, duty in percent; the controller moves in straight lines between setpoints, one switching period at a time. One duty applies to all three phases, three duties give each phase its own. A setpoint at 0 Hz switches the outputs off until the next setpoint, which restarts them with no ramp; the setpoint before a gap holds its value up to the gap.

Load the shot from a file

Typing a profile by hand is where shots go wrong. The compensation tools write the profile as a CSV (compensation/README.md); the operator console loads that file into its shot table, sends it and compares the read-back. A program should do the same: send from the file, then read every SHOT:POINt? back.

What a recall can change

*RCL puts back the supply, the shot and its tables, the phases that drive, the dead time, and the fault-input settings (which GDS:ENAble inputs are on, the polarity, the spark-gap enable). Show CONFig:PROFile:DIFF? <slot> to the operator first, and read PHASe:ENAble? and GDS:ENAble? afterwards. Nothing is recalled at boot.

Which input is in fault

GDS:LAST? replies OK <hex> <checks>: the levels of the twelve gate-driver inputs when the fault latched, bit 0 = input 01. Under NORMALLY_HIGH (the built-in polarity) the faulted inputs are the cleared bits: FFB is input 03. Read the polarity with GDS:POLarity?; do not assume it.

A reset forgets the setup

A !BOOT line can arrive at any time. The supply mode is NONE, the shot is gone, every fault input is on again, the dead time is 100 ns and the charger is off. Re-identify, tell the operator, and set up again or recall a saved profile.

Not on this chart

DEBUG:FAULT:BYPASS 1 makes the controller ignore PC10, the gate-driver inputs and the spark-gap input. It is for a bench with nothing connected and is not a recovery step. CONFig:DEADtime <ns> (50 to 3000, 100 at every boot) changes the pause between the two switches of a phase: too little risks shoot-through. Closed-loop set-up (PID:*, TARGet:*) is in docs/labview_commands.md section 4.4.

Sources: docs/labview_commands.md, docs/labview_state_and_faults.md, firmware/hbridge/docs/command_reference.md, and the HBRIDGE firmware in WHAM-CONTROLLERS. On the installed ECH-HVPS, nothing is armed or fired without the operator in charge agreeing.
